title: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
summary: An international copyright agreement adopted at a conference in Bern in 1886, dated 9 September 1886 in the UN treaty title. Its core rule gives automatic protection to works first published in other member countries. It was later revised several times, including at Paris in 1971.

as_recorded.value: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works of September 9, 1886
adopted by an international conference in Bern (Berne) in 1886

importance.justification: Foundational multilateral copyright treaty, revised repeatedly and joined by many states.
